facts.title: loss of containment at P-7111 during commissioning of replacement equipment

response.consequence: The recorded outcome was lost time injury, with 1 person injured and 4 days lost.

defences.finding: Control BUND_AND_DRAINAGE_CONTAINMENT: the secondary containment by bund and drainage had degraded below its design intent, and the root cause analysis classified this as an organisational factor.
Control EMERGENCY_ISOLATION_ON_RELEASE: the emergency isolation and depressuring on loss of containment was not in place, and the root cause analysis classified this as an individual or team action.
Control HYDROCARBON_TRANSFER_CONTROL: the controlled transfer of hydrocarbon between vessels had been bypassed, and the root cause analysis classified this as an absent or failed defence.
Control SEAL_FACE_TEMPERATURE_ALARM: the seal-face high-temperature alarm and trip was never verified as effective, and the root cause analysis classified this as an absent or failed defence.

Control SEAL_SUPPORT_SYSTEM_INTEGRITY: the integrity of the mechanical seal support system had degraded below its design intent, and the root cause analysis classified this as an absent or failed defence.

recommendations: Restore the controlled transfer of hydrocarbon between vessels on P-7111 and M-7111 and record the field verification before this task is next authorised.
Restore the seal-face high-temperature alarm and trip on P-7111 and M-7111 and record the field verification before this task is next authorised.
Restore the integrity of the mechanical seal support system on P-7111 and M-7111 and record the field verification before this task is next authorised.
response.sequence: Work was under way in maintaining sealing systems on rotating equipment, specifically setting and proving mechanical seal support systems. P-7111 (export transfer pumps) is in service for tank-to-jetty product transfer, same seal class as the Marrindal family. The task proceeded during commissioning of replacement equipment while the secondary containment by bund and drainage had degraded below its design intent. The thermal energy involved is held as hot surface, and the recorded presentation was burn, ignition, scald.
response.summary: On 3 January 2013 an incident occurred on P-7111 and M-7111 at Cape Verity Export Terminal during commissioning of replacement equipment, releasing thermal energy held as hot surface.
